lines: How We Cut Onboarding Time in Half
Maya Chen, Engineering Manager, Northwind Labs
slides.narration: Hi, I'm Maya Chen, an engineering manager at Northwind Labs. This is the story of how we cut new engineer onboarding from fourteen days to six.

lines: First merged pull request: 14 days on average
New hires waited on access and context
slides.narration: Last year a new engineer needed fourteen days on average to merge their first pull request. Most of that time was spent waiting for access and hunting for context.

lines: Change 1: a buddy for every new hire
One named buddy, 30 minutes a day, first two weeks
slides.narration: The first change was simple. Every new hire gets one named buddy, who spends thirty minutes a day with them for the first two weeks.

lines: Change 2: a sandbox account on day one
Staging data and sample tickets, no waiting for permissions
slides.narration: Second, we created a sandbox account that is ready on day one, with staging data and a few sample tickets, so nobody waits for permissions.

lines: New hires show what they built, however small
slides.narration: Third, every Friday new hires give a short demo of what they built that week, however small. It makes progress visible.
The results are on this slide. The first merged pull request now takes six days. The survey numbers at the bottom surprised us the most.
Not everything worked. A forty page wiki was mostly ignored, and recorded lectures without exercises did not help.

lines: Remove waiting first, then add people
slides.narration: My main takeaway: remove waiting first, then add people. Thank you.
